mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening cycle, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during a high-inflation environment when real rates do not rise.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of 2% or more signals weakening household demand, which reduces corporate revenue growth and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the GDP decline is accompanied by a simultaneous surge in industrial production.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) that rises above 5.5% while payrolls (PAYEMS) simultaneously contract signals a deteriorating labor market, reducing consumer purchasing power and corporate margin potential, which drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of strong productivity growth.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained two-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) of at least 1.5% signals weakening manufacturing activity, which compresses earnings expectations and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for two consecutive months by ≥1.5%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the decline is accompanied by a simultaneous surge in consumer confidence.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) of 10% or more over three months signals a housing market contraction, which reduces construction-related economic activity and drags on equities sensitive to housing demand, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls for three consecutive months by ≥10%
failure_condition: S&P 500 posts positive 60-day returns in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the housing decline is offset by strong gains in non-housing consumer spending.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in CPIAUCSL above 4% and an increase in FEDFUNDS above 3.5% within the same month signals a dual shock of higher inflation and tighter policy, which erodes real purchasing power and raises discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL > 4% AND FEDFUNDS > 3.5% in the same month
regime_hint: high inflation and restrictive policy regime
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when the economy is in a strong growth surprise.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 4% for four consecutive months, regardless of other conditions, signals persistent labor market weakness and reduces corporate earnings power, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 65% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails during periods of rapid technological adoption that boost productivity.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) of at least 1% each signals a broad-based collapse in household demand, which depresses corporate revenues and equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 and HOUST both fall by ≥1% in the same month (always-on)
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails when the decline is offset by a surge in export demand.
